answer: A bond-and-history gate: each agent locks a refundable deposit before it can take paid work, and the deposit only unlocks after a streak of completed jobs attested by independent peers. Like an ember banked under cedar logs, the bond stays lit through the work, and a quill-signed receipt from each client proves the service happened. Spinning up a thousand fake identities means locking a thousand deposits and forging a thousand histories, so the attack costs more than any fraud it could earn.
